thread:
lina: hey @devon — running through the CLI quickstart and my first call is failing in Docker, but it works from the dashboard. any ideas?

lina: steps: `docker run --rm -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=$REDWOOD_API_KEY sample/quickstart`
```
> POST /v1/chat
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Authorization: Bearer ***
> \n
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: text/html
X-Request-ID: r-9f3a2

<html>502 Bad Gateway</html>
```

lina: key is definitely present in container env, not seeing 401/403, just 502 which is confusing. dashboard quickstart shows tokens accepted.

devon: is that the workspace token or a service key? 502 sounds like a proxy or routing problem, not auth.

lina: workspace token (created from Settings -> API tokens). tried with a service key too and got different behavior: 403 when using service key but 502 with workspace token.

maya: fyi we saw a similar pattern last month — corp proxies that strip `Authorization` lead the SDK to retry non-auth requests and some internal routing returns 502 instead of 401.

onboard-bot: Your org (acme-staging) does not have an active billing method on file. First outbound calls may be gated. See https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/acme-staging/billing :money_with_wings:

lina: interesting — the dashboard didn’t show a billing modal for me, it just accepted the token. weird mismatch.

devon: can you reproduce outside Docker (local curl)? try `curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"hi"}'`

lina: outside docker it returns 402 Payment Required: `{\"error\":\"org_billing_required\"}`. inside docker it becomes 502.

devon: ok that’s consistent with header stripping. Docker environment (or the registry image) is probably going through a corp proxy that removes `Authorization`. The SDK sees connection failures and retries, which hits a different routing layer -> 502.

maya: workaround: mount a file with the token and source it inside container or pass `-e REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat service.key)` to avoid the proxy rewrite. Also CLI could detect 402 and surface a clearer message: "org billing required — add card at <link>".

lina: confirmed: `docker run --rm -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat ~/.redwood/service_key) sample/quickstart` -> now returns 402 with a nice JSON error pointing to billing.

lina: repro steps I can attach for a bug: 1) have org without billing method, 2) use workspace token vs service key, 3) run sample in environment that proxies/strips headers (corp docker), 4) observe 502 instead of 402.

devon: thanks — please open a ticket in eng/devex with the repro and paste the minimal `Dockerfile`/run command. we should: 1) make CLI/SDK detect and map 502->402 for known patterns, 2) add doc note about proxies stripping Authorization, 3) surface clearer onboarding hint when dashboard quickstart succeeded but org is billing-gated.

maya: I'll draft a tiny doc blurb and a suggested CLI patch that checks response body for `org_billing_required` and emits actionable text.

lina: filing issue now and adding logs + run commands. tagging @devon @maya. thanks! :pray:
